extraction.name: FLORES-101
extraction.description: A multilingual machine translation evaluation benchmark consisting of 3001 sentences sampled from English Wikipedia and professionally translated into 101 languages. It is designed for low-resource and many-to-many multilingual translation evaluation with multilingually aligned translations.
extraction.creator: Naman Goyal, Cynthia Gao, Vishrav Chaudhary, Peng-Jen Chen, Guillaume Wenzek, Da Ju, Sanjana Krishnan, Marc’Aurelio Ranzato, Francisco Guzmán, Angela Fan
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was built in three phases: extracting source sentences from English Wikipedia/Wikimedia sources, running pilot experiments to design the translation process, and then launching a professional translation workflow for over 100 languages. Sentence selection involved randomly selecting articles and manually choosing contiguous sentences and metadata by annotators.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Source data consisted of 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and other Wikimedia sources, specifically Wikinews, Wikijunior, and WikiVoyage, along with metadata such as URL, topic, entity links, and images.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Sentences were professionally translated in 101 languages through a carefully controlled workflow. For each target language, a Language Service Provider (LSP) produced translations, automatic checks were applied, failed translations were sent back for re-translation, and passing translations were sent to another LSP for human evaluation; if quality was insufficient, they were returned for re-translation and could go through multiple evaluation rounds.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Annotation quality was assessed through automatic checks and human evaluation, with iterative re-translation when quality was insufficient.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: For the manual sentence selection and sub-topic labeling, 10 annotators in the lab participated: 6 male and 4 female, with roles including researchers (scientists and engineers) and program/project managers, from East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America, and North America.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Automatic checks were used on translations before human evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark is biased toward English Wikipedia content, which may not represent all domains or language communities equally.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes limitations in low-resource MT evaluation generally, including low language coverage, restricted domains, low quality from automatic construction, and difficulty ensuring translator availability and quality in low-resource languages.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to support progress for low-resource languages, which could benefit speakers of those languages who are underserved by current translation systems.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation benchmark for machine translation, especially low-resource and many-to-many multilingual translation; enables assessment of model quality and comparison across 10,100 language pairs.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is publicly released, but no explicit maintenance, versioning, update schedule, or deprecation policy is described in the provided text.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Balanced sampling of paragraph locations across articles; roughly one third of paragraphs were sampled from the beginning, one third from the middle, and one third from the end.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Sentences were extracted from Wikimedia sources by randomly selecting articles and manually selecting 3–5 contiguous sentences, while avoiding very short or malformed sentences; one paragraph per document was chosen from the beginning, middle, or end.

description.evidence: We present the FLORES-101 benchmark, consisting of 3001 sentences sampled from English Wikipedia and professionally translated in 101 languages.

creator.evidence: Naman Goyal, Cynthia Gao, Vishrav Chaudhary, Peng-Jen Chen, Guillaume Wenzek, Da Ju, Sanjana Krishnan, Marc’Aurelio Ranzato, Francisco Guzmán, Angela Fan

isLiveDataset.evidence: consisting of 3001 sentences sampled from English Wikipedia and professionally translated in 101 languages

rai:dataCollection.evidence: “the overall construction process consisted of three phases... First, we extracted sentences to translate from English Wikipedia. Second, we designed and ran pilot experiments to determine the translation process, and finally we launched the actual translation workflow for over 100 languages.”

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: “The sentence selection process consisted of selecting an article at random from each source, and then manually selecting a few (typically between 3 and 5) contiguous sentences from each article”

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: “All source sentences were extracted from multiple Wikimedia sources” and “we collected a third of the sentences from Wikinews... a third from Wikijunior... and a third from WikiVoyage”

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: “These sentences have been translated in 101 languages by professional translators through a carefully controlled process.” and “For each target language, sentences are translated by a translation Language Service Provider (LSP). The resulting translations are automatically checked. If these checks fail, translations are sent back for re-translation. If the automatic checks pass, translations are sent to another LSP for human evaluation. If the quality is not sufficient, translations are sent back to the original translation LSP for re-translation. Depending on the human score, the process can repeat for multiple rounds of human evaluation.”

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: “The resulting translations are automatically checked. If these checks fail, translations are sent back for re-translation. If the automatic checks pass, translations are sent to another LSP for human evaluation. If the quality is not sufficient, translations are sent back to the original translation LSP for re-translation.”

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: “The selection process was performed by 10 different annotators in our lab, 6 male and 4 female; with different roles in research: researchers (scientists and engineers) and program/project managers; originally coming from different regions of the world: East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America and North America.”

rai:dataBiases.evidence: consisting of 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and covering a variety of different topics and domains

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: These often have very low coverage of low-resource languages... There are some benchmarks that have high coverage, but these are often in specific domains... or have low quality because they are built using automatic approaches... Working with professional translators in low-resource languages is difficult because of their scarce availability, and because it is non-trivial to check the quality of their work

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: the majority of the world’s population speak low-resource languages and would benefit from improvements in translation quality on their native languages

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: we introduce the FLORES-101 evaluation benchmark... The resulting dataset enables better assessment of model quality on the long tail of low-resource languages, including the evaluation of many-to-many multilingual translation systems... it enables seamless evaluation of 10,100 language pairs

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: By publicly releasing such a high-quality and high-coverage dataset

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: “We balanced the location selection to be equally distributed across the whole corpus — roughly one third of paragraphs were sampled from the beginning of the article, one third from the middle, and so on.”

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: “The sentence selection process consisted of selecting an article at random from each source, and then manually selecting a few (typically between 3 and 5) contiguous sentences from each article, avoiding segments with very short or malformed sentences. To avoid bias coming from the document structure, we carefully selected one paragraph per document, from either the beginning, middle or end of the article.”
